verdict: 1M-context single-case multineedle is NOT executable on this 4x GB10 TP=4 deployment as configured: the KV fill during a 1M-token prefill consumes ~9 GiB of host-side unified memory per node by ~50% progress (520K tokens), colliding with the ~9-10 GiB post-launch host floor. Three attempts on progressively leaner configurations all hit the identical wall (~515-521K tokens pending, MemAvailable <500 MiB, NVRM NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY): (1) prod 1m profile 1100000 max-total-tokens with desktop stack, (2) corrected lane profile 1049088 max-total-tokens + max_running_requests=1 with desktop stack, (3) same lane profile headless (gdm stopped, GNOME gone). Attempt 3 proves the desktop stack is NOT the cause: the wall is the model's own KV allocation profile. Attempt 2's abort at nearly the same prefill depth headless confirms reproducibility.
methodology: chat API, thinking off, temp 0, max_tokens 128, needles at 33%/66% depth, filler calibrated 0.1390 tok/char on live tokenizer, 14 GiB client-side pre-submit memory gate (passed every attempt), background watch with NVRM trigger
node_recovery: all four nodes returned to 116-120 GiB MemAvailable after each teardown; no reboots required
paths_forward: chunked-prefill microbatch KV spilling (requires engine support for host KV offload at 1M ctx on this architecture)
a 2-case split harness that prefills in two radix-cached halves (needs prefix-cache hit across requests — untested here)
serving the lane from a node with fewer host residents does not help (attempt 3)
